info.title: YuviPep AI Sales Platform
info.description: Zero-touch sales automation backend — multi-organisation, AI-agent driven. Every request is organisation-scoped; every client message needs a one-tap human approval.

post.description:
Exchange a still-valid token for a fresh one (G4 — lets the mobile
app extend a session without re-entering the password). An expired
token cannot refresh: get_current_user already rejects it.

Store the user's own Gmail App Password (encrypted) so their proposals
and messages send from their personal address.

post.description:
Forgotten password (mobile G6): the admin issues a fresh temporary
password — shown once — and the user must change it at next login.
Creates a NEW pricing version; old proposals keep the version they used.

Advisory only. Nothing is saved: the administrator accepts, rewords or
rejects each suggestion, then PUTs the plan.

Fill the plan with obviously-fake sample values and return the PDF.

No model is called: a preview must not spend tokens, and it must look the
same every time an administrator presses the button.

get.description:
Serve one image out of the stored document.

`name` is checked against the media list the outline recorded, so the route
cannot be walked to another part of the package or off disk.

delete.description:
`code` is UNIQUE per org, so without this a typo is permanent — and its
description keeps being read by the offering matcher.

No reference guard: nothing points at a message template. Removing the
last intro/email one breaks card-scan drafting, and the console's checklist
turns amber immediately — that is the guard (06_DESIGN.md §7.2).

Member rows go with it: the schema declares no `ondelete=` anywhere, so
the handler is the only thing that will clean them up.

post.description:
Bulk removal, scoped to one organisation.

Unlike scripts/reset_for_datacentre_demo.py — which deletes globally and is
safe only because the demo database holds one tenant — every statement here
carries `WHERE org_id = :org`. Tables whose org_id is nullable (jobs,
llm_usage) keep their platform-level rows, which belong to no tenant.

Business-card photo -> Vision/OCR -> saved contact -> intro message
drafted from the org template, ready for one-tap approval (doc §9.1).

Upload the recording and start the background pipeline. The app polls
GET /meetings/{id} to show progress (never a frozen screen — §11.5).
Retry a failed pipeline (poor signal / model hiccup — doc §12).
Human review of extracted items: edit, add, remove, confirm (doc §9.1.4).

Book a meeting in advance (Workflow 1.2) — mirrored to the agent's
calendar as a booking.

The manual path (recording refused, or a dictated summary): typed
notes are the transcript source, and the Planner runs the same merge —
the engines reconcile manual work, they never fight it.

Edit by simple voice or text command, e.g. 'make the workshops 16 and
the price Rs 1500 per year' (doc §9.1.10).

A human edited the rendered file outside the system and re-submits it
(mobile G3). The upload becomes the proposal's send artifact, recorded as
a revision — and it must re-pass internal review before sending. The
locked total is verified inside the PDF when its text is extractable;
a file whose numbers no longer match is refused.

The 'Approve and Send' tap: prepares (or reuses) the proposal email and
queues it immediately — sender is the salesperson's own address.

Workflow 3.4: mark ready → the org's approval rule fires (e.g. proposal
above ₹1,00,000 → sales lead approves). Below every rule it clears
immediately.

get.description:
The contract itself.

A missing PDF is converted here rather than refused. F3 leaves `pdf_path`
null when LibreOffice fails, deliberately -- losing an approved contract
over a converter hiccup is worse than converting late -- and this is where
that retry was always going to happen.

post.description:
The one-tap 'Approve & Send'.

`allow_blanks` (additive, default false — F30): a draft still carrying
`[Name]`-style blanks is refused with a 422 naming them. Passing true is
the caller saying "I have read it and I mean to send it as it is". Old
clients simply get the refusal, which is the safe direction for a build
that cannot show the blanks.
Delivery receipts from the WhatsApp Cloud API -> Message Delivery Log.
Mark done; the lead is updated and the next reminder is set (doc §9.4).

get.description:
Full-month grid (up to 31 days) with demos per date — free and busy
days at a glance (doc §9.3.4).

Replay a conversation, oldest first — so a reopened app shows the chat
the user left, not an empty screen. A conversation is private to the
person who had it: only the caller's own turns are ever returned.

Serve a stored file — storage.resolve refuses paths outside the

post.description:
Transcribe a short recording for a text field and hand the text back.

This is the keyboard, not the meeting pipeline. The two differ on purpose:

  * It runs DICTATION_WHISPER_MODEL (tiny by default), not the pipeline's
    medium — someone is watching a spinner with a half-typed field open.
  * The audio is never written to storage and never touches the database.
    A dictated word is a keystroke; keystrokes are not records, and
    keeping them would create a store of employee voice clips nobody asked
    for and retention has no rule for.
  * No permission gate beyond "logged in and in an org". Dictation is a way
    of typing, so anyone allowed to type into a field is allowed to speak
    into it — gating this on record_meeting would silently take the mic
    away from roles that can still use the keyboard.

Right to be removed: purge the person's data from the database, files
and memory store — not just hide it (doc §14).

get.description:
Which project does this conflict / plan belong to? (F58)

Notifications carry only `entity_type` + `entity_id` (Data Model §2.5), and
a conflict's screen is the project's Conflicts tab — so tapping one had
nothing to navigate with and fell through to "this opens fully in a later
phase", for a screen that has existed and worked since Act 11.

A lookup rather than a new `notifications.project_id` column: additive, no
migration, and it cannot make the 16 existing notify() call sites wrong.
The live timeline — the event stream, humanised (Workflow 17.6).

post.description:
Chain deals (Workflow 27): commercials on the parent, delivery on the
children — each child with its own lead record and plan.

Finish a task any way you like — in-app, by voice, or by uploading the
artifact you made outside. Both are first-class (Workflow 4 B.3).

'I'm blocked' stops the nudge ladder and starts the right machinery —
chase the blocker, not the blocked (Workflow 11).

'Give new date' from the nudge — the engine checks the ripple before
accepting: a break of a dependent task or client commitment routes the
change to the phase lead instead (Workflow 10.3).

Split into linked children (Workflow 16.5): parent kept, children carry
parent_item_id, second part depends on the first.

One screen, all proposed assignments — confirm-all or change any.
Recorded as assignments.status changes, never approvals rows.

Lead-only (F51). `lead_confirm` mode exists precisely so a *lead* signs off
the batch before anyone is notified; until this gate existed, any org member
could confirm the whole organisation's assignments, and an operations agent
was being offered the card on his own Home screen.

The inbound webhook (also the dry-run entry). Voice notes are
transcribed before reaching this text form.

get.description: 'Why did the AI do that?' — open to the whole organisation.

post.description:
Manual trigger of the Sync Engine's daily sweep (also runs on the
scheduler). Useful for testing and for dry-runs.

Ask the Communication Engine for a draft — it still goes through the
approval gate like every other outward message.
Amounts always derived from accepted proposals — never typed.

Draft the carrying email to the gatekeeper (CC the principal) and put
it through the approval gate (Workflow 8.3).

delete.description:
Nothing in the schema references a vendor row: no foreign key, no
id-shaped column anywhere points at `vendors.id`. The only place a vendor
is ever recorded outside its own table is `action_items.external_wait`,
a free-text JSON blob written by `POST /tasks/{id}/vendor-promise`
(`app/api/workflow.py`) as `{"vendor_name": <typed string>, ...}` — a
name, not a reference. Deleting a vendor therefore cannot orphan
anything: the vendor list is a catalogue, and a task's recorded promise
keeps its typed name, independent of whether that row still exists.

post.description:
Recording leave triggers the automatic endangered-task check
(Workflow 12).

An uploaded file is a fully valid way to finish any task — the rest of
the machine treats it exactly like a generated one.
New version per change — plans record which version generated them.

get.description:
A go-live prerequisite that had a write path and no read path: without
this a console can only overwrite task waves blindly.

delete.description:
Nothing references a playbook, so there is no reference guard. Removing
the current version promotes its predecessor — the un-supersede path the
API has never had.

post.description:
The one-tap accept: every future project inherits the lesson
(Workflow 22.5).
Changing who approves what is a settings edit — never a code change.

Skills bring work to a desk; leads adjust levels when reality proves
them wrong (Roles doc §4.5).
